utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: A very good afternoon to you all. Mr. Registrar, call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-95-5/18-R77.3, the contempt case of Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker is kindly requested to repeat because nothing could be heard because of the feedback.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-5/18-R77.3 in the contempt case of Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. I am Judge Melville Baird, a Judge of Trial Chamber (iii), and I have been designated to hear this Initial Appearance of Mr. Krstic. I would like counsel appearing for Mr. Krstic to now introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Tomislav Visnjic representing General Radislav Krstic in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. For the record, I know that the Chamber has decided to prosecute this matter itself pursuant to Rule 77(D)(ii). Now then, Mr. Krstic, are you able to hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can hear you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And are you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And are you receiving the interpretation in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Very well. I must now go through certain formalities. I must first ask you to state your full name and date and place of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Radislav Krstic. I was born on the 15th of February, 1948, in Vlasenica, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to check that you have received a copy of the Order in Lieu of Indictment, dated March 27, 2013, in your own language and that you have understood its content.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did receive it in my language and I have understood the substance of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now you are representing here today by Mr. Visnjic. Are you satisfied with your representation here today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Now then, Mr. Krstic, you are charged with one count of contempt for having refused to comply with the Chamber's subpoena of October 23rd, 2012, and the addendum to the subpoena, dated 7th November, 2012. The Chamber, having found that there were no medical reasons which amounted to good cause for you not to comply with the subpoena held that there was sufficient reason to believe that you knowingly and wilfully interfered with the administration of justice and therefore may be in contempt of the Tribunal. Well, at this stage I would ask whether it is still your position today that you are not willing to testify in the Karadzic proceedings? Now, if you would prefer, we can go in private session so that the public will not hear -- will not be able to hear what you say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For medical reasons, health reasons exclusively, I am not able to testify in the case of Mr. Karadzic before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now then, you are entitled to have the Order in Lieu of Indictment read out to you in court today, but you may choose to dispense with that. Now, do you wish it to be read now or do you waive that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is up to you to decide. I have read the Order in Lieu of Indictment, studied it, I have understood it completely, so as far as I am concerned there is no need for it to be read again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: All right. So in effect you have waived that right, in effect. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii) of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you can enter a plea to the charge of contempt set out in the Order in Lieu of Indictment today, if you so choose, or you can decide to postpone your plea for a period of up to ten days in accordance Rule 77(E). Now, did you discuss this with your counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not discuss this particular matter with my counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Would -- Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this refers only to the dead-line. At least as far as I understood from my conversation with the General, he is prepared to plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me -- let me get it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But perhaps we can ask him again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Indeed. Indeed. Pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii) of our rules of procedure, you can enter a plea to the charge of contempt set out in the Order in Lieu of Indictment today, if you so choose, or you can decide to postpone your plea for up to a period of ten days in accordance with Rule 77(E). Now then, do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: And how do you wish to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. I would like to plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Krstic, rise please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You are charged with contempt of Court under Rule 77(A)(i) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: In light of the nature of the charge against you and all the circumstances, the Chamber would like to have this matter resolved as quickly as possible. Given your plea, this means setting a date for the trial. At the end of all the evidence, the Chamber will issue its judgement. Now, at the trial you would be entitled to call witnesses and you may choose to testify yourself. This is for you to discuss with your counsel. I would therefore like to ask you, through your counsel, how long you consider you will need to prepare for this trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, without going into too much detail, I believe that we will be ready in 30 or 35 days. We need to obtain some documents, and taking into account the translation and everything I think we are talking about a period of 30, 35 to 40 days to be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: There is no question of a figure below that at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we obtain the documents. We are clear about what we need to obtain, but there are two ways to proceed. Perhaps we can shorten the trial time, which is why we would prefer to perhaps get written evidence rather than calling a live witness. The second path would be obtaining documents from a foreign country, so if we embark on that right now it's possible that we would obtain that without the use of Rule 54, which would be a direct request for documents. We are talking about a transcript of a trial, so we are hoping to get this as soon as possible. However, I have still have not any kind of date by which we would be able to obtain that. So this is why I set the period of 30 to 40 days. If we obtain the documents within the next two weeks, I can inform you about that, and then you could proceed to issue an order setting the date for the trial if things should happen that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: The whole question of your Defence is entirely in your hands. Now, as this is a contempt case, I do not believe that there might be issues of disclosure or that these proceedings should be prolonged unnecessarily. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. If you wish to file any preliminary motions, you are ordered to do so within ten days from today in accordance Rule 77(E). Now, once these deadlines have passed, the Chamber will consider the court schedule and set a date for trial as soon as possible thereafter. Thank you. Now, Mr. Krstic, I am aware that you have certain medical conditions, and I wish to ask you whether your medical condition has been adequately provided for in the United Nations Detention Unit and whether you have any other concerns with respect to the Detention Unit. Should you wish to mention any private details concerning your medical situation, we can of course go into private session so that those details remain confidential.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to say regarding my status and also my treatment by the medical staff in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Now, Mr. Krstic, and indeed you, Mr. Visnjic, do you have any other matter which you wish to raise at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Not at this time, other than wanting to say that I am going to inform you in writing about our endeavours to obtain these documents for purposes of planning the beginning of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you very much indeed. All right. This being the case, without anything further to be raised, the hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: sine die

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.46 p.m.
